title: Build every chart in one anatomy, from evidence label to table.
rule: Every chart prints the same eight parts in the same order, so a reader always knows where to look: the evidence label and grade line (Rules 13.1 and 13.2), the title, the measure line (Rule 13.7), the reading guide, the chart, its notes, the source line (Rule 13.6) and the table (Rule 14.13).

The title is one full sentence, and house rule H08 sizes its claim. The reading guide says in a sentence or two how to read the drawing. Notes carry what the drawing cannot. A part with nothing to say is left out, and the rest keep their order.

text: Readers learn where things are after a few charts. When every chart puts its source in the same place, a reader can check any figure in seconds, and a chart that lacks a part shows the gap.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Fill every word field of the spec, as the kit’s README sets out under “The keys a spec takes”; the kit prints the parts in this order and leaves out an empty one.

correct.caption: The eight parts in order, each numbered where the kit prints it. The table sits folded under the source line.
correct.alt: A finished chart with each of its eight parts numbered in reading order: Evidence label and grade line, Title, Measure line, Reading guide, Chart, Notes, Source line, Table. Its title: Civic and social organizations employed 201,423 people in March 2023, about 113,300 fewer than in 1998.
correct.notes: The numerals are drawn by the plate's style on the kit's own parts, so they follow the figure as the kit prints it.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 14.2. The title names a topic and states no finding, and the chart drops its label, measure line, notes and source line, so a reader cannot tell what was counted or who counted it.
failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same line under a title that names only the topic, with no label, measure line, notes or source line.
